claims.claim_text: The PyTorch Foundation announced the release of PyTorch 2.15 on October 28, 2026.
claims.excerpt: We are excited to announce the release of PyTorch® 2.15 (release notes)!

claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 is composed of 3,117 commits from 583 contributors since PyTorch 2.14.
claims.excerpt: This release is composed of 3,117 commits from 583 contributors since PyTorch 2.14.

claims.claim_text: In PyTorch 2.15 the rewritten NCCL backend becomes the default for every nccl process group, with TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 and the nccl-legacy backend name as rollback paths.
claims.excerpt: In 2.15 it is the default for every nccl process group, with TORCH_DIST_USE_NCCL2=0 and the nccl-legacy backend name as rollback paths.

claims.claim_text: A backend-agnostic flight recorder writes a post-mortem to disk when a collective hangs.
claims.excerpt: a backend-agnostic flight recorder writes a post-mortem to disk when a collective hangs

claims.claim_text: torch.distributed gains a Python transport API for one-sided data movement, with NIXL as the first backend.
claims.excerpt: torch.distributed gains a Python transport API for one-sided data movement, with NIXL as the first backend.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch says the new MPS grouped_mm gemv path gives 1.32–1.34x higher MoE decode throughput on an M3 Ultra, and that MPS now supports torch.float8_e4m3fn.
claims.excerpt: the new MPS grouped_mm has a gemv path that gives 1.32–1.34x higher MoE decode throughput on an M3 Ultra

claims.claim_text: NVGEMM now folds the NVFP4 dequantization factor into the GEMM, removing a separate pointwise launch per layer during decode on Blackwell.
claims.excerpt: now folds the scalar dequantization factor of ModelOpt NVFP4 linear layers into the GEMM, removing a separate pointwise launch per layer during decode

claims.claim_text: The default PyTorch wheel moves to CUDA 13.2, with CUDA 13.4 wheels shipping alongside it that add experimental support for NVIDIA Rubin GPUs.
claims.excerpt: The CUDA 13.4 wheels add experimental support for NVIDIA Rubin GPUs.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 adds ROCm 10.0 wheels and preview support including Tensor Data Mover for AMD gfx1250 (MI450).
claims.excerpt: PyTorch 2.15 adds ROCm 10.0 wheels alongside the ROCm 7.14 wheels introduced in 2.14.

claims.claim_text: PyTorch 2.15 drops support for Python 3.10, requiring Python 3.11 or newer, and requires macOS 15 or newer for MPS acceleration.
claims.excerpt: Python 3.10 is no longer supported. PyTorch 2.15 requires Python 3.11 or newer
